narrative.text: Describes the CoronaVac vaccine and its efficacy in trials, including 51% against symptomatic infection in Brazil and higher protection against severe disease in Indonesia and Turkey. It reports real-world effectiveness from a national cohort in Chile against illness, hospitalization, intensive care and death, and discusses older adults, booster doses and co-administration. The section also covers the recommended two-dose schedule, contraindications and precautions such as post-vaccination observation and delaying vaccination during fever.

Gives CoronaVac recommendations for specific groups, including older adults with a booster after 4-6 months, people with comorbidities, and pregnant and breastfeeding women. It states that routine use under age 18 is not recommended pending emergency listing and covers people with HIV or immunosuppression, prior infection and those treated with antibodies.

Advises prioritizing vaccination in crowded settings such as camps, prisons and slums and addressing inequities in access. It explains that antibody tests cannot distinguish past infection from vaccination, that other public health measures must continue, and that programme planning should weigh equity and feasibility.

Lists the post-authorization research and monitoring WHO recommends for CoronaVac, covering safety surveillance of serious adverse events, effectiveness against variants and in older people, booster schedules and effects on transmission. It ends with the acknowledgements of SAGE experts and WHO staff.
The reference list of the CoronaVac guidance, citing WHO SAGE documents and clinical studies on the vaccine, followed by a note that the Russian text translates the WHO English original.

The opening page of WHO interim recommendations (in Russian) on using Sinovac's inactivated COVID-19 vaccine CoronaVac, issued in May 2021 and updated in October 2021 and March 2022. It explains that the guidance rests on SAGE recommendations and evidence reviews, and describes the methods and disclaimers.
